fieldValues.title: One essay home: a URL that says who is in charge and opens an essay
fieldValues.move: The essay editor gets its own front door: essay.semanticops.com (and /essay on the app host) serves a home page instead of the generic open-a-repository landing. The page says, in the editor's own help words, that the writer owns every word and the AI supports; that a new essay lives in the browser until the writer chooses where to save it, and what the save choices are; how to connect an AI; and offers a one-click new essay and two or three example essays. The words are help records in the bundled help repository (the same records a paired agent reads through ui_help once an essay is open), so the page is edited in the editor, never in code. Examples are ordinary .srsj files opened by the existing read-only link, with the essay editor offered on that link and Save a copy… as the way to make one your own; each example explains itself in its purpose field.
fieldValues.does_not_fix: The reference library, quote browsing and the agent-guided domain → personas → problems → remedies → claims process (SP-85, SP-57, SP-101; exercise in this commit). Whether the editor's concepts are fewer or simpler (SP-130's first remedy 44a6f76d). The repository-level first view (SP-119). Agents cannot read the home page itself, only its words once an essay is open.
fieldValues.falsifier: A cold visitor given only https://essay.semanticops.com, in a fresh browser, still cannot say in one sentence what the editor is for, or cannot start writing and find where their essay is saved, without asking.
fieldValues.return_when: When three people outside the programme have been sent the URL and the owner has heard what they did first and where they stopped.
